data.summary: Materialize a workflow output and complete the execution when no legacy continuation is connected.

outletDocs.description: Optional continuation past END. With none, the run completes at END, and a caller waiting on this workflow resumes only if it wired the output END selects.
outletDocs.fires: After END materializes its output. Every default edge fires, in stored order; none wired completes the workflow.

branches.when: Optional. Write exactly 'default'; the engine selects the edge by type, not by handle.

notes: Only author one in a workflow another workflow calls through a SKILL node with output edges (or in a tool / marketplace package). A workflow nobody waits on ends when a branch runs out of edges; END adds nothing there.

The value returned is what a CODE node stored before it with $output.set("<output name>", value). END does not read the output schema: without that call the value is undefined, nothing is written, and the caller reads whatever $memory.response held before.
$output.set only accepts names of declared outputs, and only the part before the first dot.
Point several END nodes at the same output when several paths end the same way.
Deleting an output also deletes the END nodes that select it; the server refuses while a caller still has an edge on it.
Shapes you will meet when reading pulled workflows: v2 { outputId } (this one) and v3 { type: 'success' | 'error', value } in legacy AI_TASK sub-workflows.
Brain V5 accepts only outputId and optional DLP settings; the historical type/value surface is not part of this revision.
Default candidates fan out in stored order and an absent candidate terminates the workflow.
A channel workflow with no declared outputs never has an END: a branch ends when it runs out of edges (end_without_declared_outputs).
Precondition: The Brain V5 output identity is meaningful for the current workflow snapshot.

rules: Never write a START node. The tool adds the workflow's one START (`validate --fix` and `jelou push` write it), unless the workflow enters only through a WEBHOOK.
Your first edge is { "sourceId": "START", "targetId": "<first-node>", "branch": "default" }. "START" is a reserved alias the tool resolves to the real START id; no other node may use that id.
The first node cannot be START, WEBHOOK, EMPTY, NOTE.
WEBHOOK is optional, at most one per workflow, and never chained to START.

A workflow or tool that enters only through a WEBHOOK needs no START: write no edge from "START" and the tool adds none. A channel message or a TOOL node never starts it then. A marketplace skill always needs START.
Next to a wired WEBHOOK that feeds the flow, a START with no edge is only a warning: the tool wires nothing to it and push keeps it.
